title: Hari Om Shukla v. State of U.P. — s.135 FIR not quashed
coram: V.K. Shukla, J.; Shashi Kant, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 12546 of 2014
disposition: s.135 FIR not quashed; CrPC 41/41-A on arrest; compounding under Supply Code
headnote: A criminal writ to quash an FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 was refused where the FIR disclosed a cognizable offence. Any arrest for an offence not entailing more than seven years must follow Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Hari Om Shukla approached the Allahabad High Court to quash FIR dated 31 May 2014, registered as Case Crime No. 138 of 2014 under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 at Police Station Shivli, District Kanpur Dehat. He had not been arrested. Counsel argued that the alleged offence could not attract a sentence exceeding seven years, so arrest should not be mechanical, and that the offence was compoundable under the electricity law.

holding_units.holding: An FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence is not to be quashed. Arrest, if effectuated for an offence not entailing a sentence of more than seven years, must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Grant of compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Pointed to the Code remedy if the offence is compoundable; no decision on entitlement.
